title.en: A Day in 2889 of an American Journalist

text.en: How might a newspaper owner's day look a thousand years from now?

This science-fiction story by Jules Verne imagines the year 2889 in a city called Centropolis, the new name of New York. An American newspaper owner lives with gadgets such as the phonotelephote, which carries both voice and picture, and phototelegrams, which send pictures by telegraph.
The story predicts technologies that look surprisingly like today's video calls. It reminds us that science fiction imagines the future from present knowledge.
Glossary words: phonotelephote, phototelegram, valet, Jovians and inhabitants. Learn how writers describe future inventions.
